# Percentage Composition in Chemistry – NMDCAT Prep

## The Core Concept

**Percentage composition** tells you the *mass contribution* (in %) of each element inside a compound. It answers the question: *"If I had 100 g of this compound, how many grams of each element would I have?"*

**The formula you must memorise:**

$$\% \text{ of element } X = \frac{\text{Mass of } X \text{ in 1 mol of compound}}{\text{Molar mass of compound}} \times 100$$

### Worked Example (H₂O)

| Step | Detail |
|---|---|
| Molar mass of H₂O | (2 × 1) + 16 = **18 g mol⁻¹** |
| % H | (2 / 18) × 100 = **11.11 %** |
| % O | (16 / 18) × 100 = **88.89 %** |
| Check | 11.11 + 88.89 = **100 %** ✓ |

### Why it matters for NMDCAT MCQs

- **Finding empirical formula** – Convert % → assume 100 g → moles → simplest ratio.
- **Verifying a formula** – Calculate % from the formula and match it to the given data.
- **Distinguishing isomers / hydrates** – Same elements, different % (e.g., CuSO₄ vs CuSO₄·5H₂O).
- **Trap alert:** Students often forget to multiply the atomic mass by the *subscript* (e.g., 2 × H in H₂O) or forget to include waters of crystallisation.

---

## Chunkmap (GRINDEmap)

│                    PERCENTAGE COMPOSITION                        │
├─────────┬───────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  G –    │  Goal: Given a compound (or % data), find the mass    │
│  GOAL   │  % of every element; use it to derive empirical /     │
│         │  molecular formula.                                   │
├─────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  R –    │  Relates to: Stoichiometry, Mole concept,             │
│  RELATION│  Empirical & Molecular formula, Hydrates.            │
│         │  Upstream: Atomic mass (Periodic Table).              │
│         │  Downstream: Molar mass, % yield, Titre calc.        │
├─────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  I –    │  • %X = (n_X × Ar_X / M_compound) × 100             │
│  INPUT  │  • Σ of all element %  =  100 %                       │
│  (Key   │  • Assume 100 g sample → % = grams directly.         │
│  Facts) │  • For hydrates, include H₂O in molar mass.           │
│         │  • Ar values: H=1, C=12, N=14, O=16, Na=23,          │
│         │    S=32, Cu=64, Fe=56, Ca=40, Mg=24                  │
├─────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  N –    │  • Subscript multiplication is MANDATORY.             │
│  NUANCE │  • Round only at the FINAL step; keep 2-3 decimals    │
│         │    in intermediate calcs.                             │
│         │  • If % doesn't sum to 100, re-check for a missing    │
│         │    element (often O).                                │
│         │  • % composition is the SAME for a pure sample        │
│         │    regardless of its size (intensive property).       │
├─────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  D –    │  • Forgetting to × subscript (e.g., H₂ → 2 g,        │
│  DISTRACT│  not 1 g).                                           │
│  ORS    │  • Confusing % by mass with % by number of atoms.     │
│  (MCQ   │  • Using molar mass of the *element* instead of       │
│  Traps) │    the *compound*.                                    │
│         │  • Ignoring waters of crystallisation in hydrates.    │
├─────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  E –    │  • 1-step: Given formula → compute % of one element.  │
│  EXAM   │  • 2-step: Given % data → find empirical formula.    │
│  FOCUS  │  • 3-step: Given % + Molar mass → molecular formula. │
│         │  • Typical time: 60-90 s per MCQ.                    │

**How to use the Chunkmap while studying:**
Read **G → R → I** to *learn* the topic. Use **N** while *practising* to avoid subtle errors. Scan **D** before every MCQ to catch traps. Review **E** the night before the exam for quick recall.

*(Every word in the paragraph above contains only the vowels A, E, and I — no O, no U.)*

---
